- name: int_lever__posting_analytics
      description: Job posting performance and engagement analytics (one row per posting with application, interview, conversion, timing, and scoring metrics)
      grain: One row per posting_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__posting
      - staging.stg_lever__application
      - staging.stg_lever__interview
      - staging.stg_lever__interviewer_user
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity
      - staging.stg_lever__stage
      business_logic: 'Build one row per posting_id by enriching posting attributes with application, interview, hiring, time-efficiency, and scoring metrics. 1) Posting base - From staging.stg_lever__posting: select posting_id, posting_title, categories_* (department, team, location, level, commitment), state as posting_state, created_at, creator_user_id, owner_user_id. 2) Application metrics (grouped by posting_id from staging.stg_lever__application) - total_applications: distinct applications. - unique_candidates: distinct candidates. - unique_opportunities: distinct opportunities. - referred_applications: distinct applications with a referrer_user_id present. - internal_applications: distinct applications where type is ''user''. - first_application_date: earliest application created_at; last_application_date: latest application created_at. - Conditional counts only include rows that meet the condition; missing IDs are not counted. 3) Interview metrics (via applications) - Join applications to interviews on opportunity_id; left join interviewer users on interview_id. - total_interviews_scheduled: distinct interviews. - completed_interviews: distinct interviews not canceled. - canceled_interviews: distinct interviews that were canceled. - unique_interviewers: distinct interviewer users. - avg_interview_duration_minutes: average of interview duration. - total_interview_time_minutes: sum of interview duration. 4) Hiring outcomes (via opportunities and stages) - Join applications to opportunities; left join stages. - candidates_hired: distinct opportunities whose stage name contains "hire" or "accept" (case-insensitive). - offers_extended: distinct opportunities whose stage name contains "offer" (case-insensitive). - candidates_rejected: distinct opportunities that are archived. 5) Time efficiency (via opportunities) - Join applications to opportunities. - Keep only rows where last_advanced_at and application created_at exist. - For each kept row, compute day differences: • to advancement: days between last_advanced_at and application created_at • to last contact: days between last_interaction_at and application created_at (missing last_interaction_at are ignored in averages) - Aggregate per posting_id: • avg_days_to_advancement: mean days to advancement • avg_days_to_last_contact: mean days to last contact over the same filtered set • median_days_to_advancement: 50th percentile of days to advancement 6) Final derivations (left-join metrics to posting base by posting_id; fill missing metrics with 0 where noted) - referral_rate_pct: referred_applications / total_applications × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_applications = 0. - internal_application_rate_pct: internal_applications / total_applications × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_applications = 0. - interview_completion_rate_pct: completed_interviews / total_interviews_scheduled × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_interviews_scheduled = 0. - application_to_hire_rate_pct: candidates_hired / total_applications × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 if total_applications = 0. - offer_acceptance_rate_pct: candidates_hired / offers_extended × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if offers_extended = 0. - avg_days_to_advancement, avg_days_to_last_contact, median_days_to_advancement: set to 0 if no qualifying rows. - days_to_first_application: days between posting_created_at and first_application_date when both exist; otherwise null. - posting_effectiveness_score (0–100): • min(20, total_applications) • +25 if candidates_hired > 0 • +20 if avg_days_to_advancement ≤ 30; +10 if ≤ 60; else +0 • +15 if interview_completion_rate_pct ≥ 80; else +5 • +10 if referral_rate_pct ≥ 20; +5 if ≥ 10; else +0 • +10 if offer_acceptance_rate_pct ≥ 70; else +0 Round to 0 decimals and clamp between 0 and 100. - performance_tier (first match): • High Performing: total_applications ≥ 20 AND candidates_hired ≥ 2 AND avg_days_to_advancement ≤ 45 (treat missing as 999) • Good Performing: total_applications ≥ 10 AND candidates_hired ≥ 1 AND avg_days_to_advancement ≤ 60 (treat missing as 999) • Moderate Performing: total_applications ≥ 5 • Low Performing: total_applications ≥ 1 • Else: No Applications - primary_bottleneck (first match): • total_applications = 0 → No Attraction - Poor Job Posting • interview_completion_rate_pct < 70 → Interview Scheduling Issues • offer_acceptance_rate_pct < 60 AND offers_extended > 0 → Low Offer Acceptance • avg_days_to_advancement > 60 → Slow Decision Process • candidates_hired = 0 AND total_applications ≥ 10 → High Standards or Poor Fit • Else → No Major Issues - calculated_at: current timestamp at run time (time zone aware). - Final output is ordered by posting_effectiveness_score descending, then total_applications descending.'

        - not_null
        - unique

      - name: unique_candidates

      - name: internal_application_rate_pct

        description: Total interview duration in minutes; 0 if no interviews

      - name: avg_days_to_last_contact

      - name: median_days_to_advancement
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Median (50th percentile) days from application to last advancement; 0 if none
      - name: days_to_first_application
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Days from posting_created_at to the first application; NULL if either timestamp is missing
      - name: posting_effectiveness_score
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Composite 0–100 score from application volume, hires, speed, interview completion, referrals, and offer acceptance; rounded to 0 decimals and clamped
      - name: performance_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Tier assigned from thresholds on applications, hires, and average days to advancement
      - name: primary_bottleneck
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Primary bottleneck based on ordered checks: attraction, interview completion, offer acceptance, decision speed, or fit/standards'

        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Current timestamp when the row is computed (time zone aware)

- name: int_lever__posting_performance
      description: Job posting performance metrics by posting, including applications, candidates, interviews, conversion rates, score, and status
      grain: One row per posting_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__posting
      - staging.stg_lever__application
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity
      - staging.stg_lever__stage
      - staging.stg_lever__contact_email
      - staging.stg_lever__contact_phone
      - staging.stg_lever__resume
      - staging.stg_lever__interview
      business_logic: 'For each posting in staging.stg_lever__posting: - Left join applications on posting_id; left join opportunities on application.opportunity_id; left join contact_email/phone on opportunity.contact_id; left join resume on application.opportunity_id; left join interview on application.opportunity_id. - All counting metrics use unique counts to avoid double-counting from joins. - Application metrics: - total_applications = unique applications; unique_candidates = unique candidates; unique_opportunities = unique opportunities. - first_application_date = earliest application.created_at; last_application_date = latest application.created_at; both null when no applications. - referred_applications = unique applications with a referrer. - internal_applications = unique applications where type is user; external_applications = unique applications where type is candidate. - referral_rate = if total_applications > 0 then referred_applications ÷ total_applications × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; otherwise 0. - Time metric: - days_to_first_application = fractional days between posting_created_at and first_application_date; computed only when both timestamps can be parsed; otherwise null. - Stage-based candidate metrics (stage membership determined by stage_name keywords, case-insensitive): - Interview-like: stage_name contains interview, technical, or onsite; Offer-like: contains offer; Hire-like: contains hire or accept. - candidates_reached_interview/offer/hired = unique opportunities currently in the corresponding stage group. - active_candidates_30d = unique opportunities with last_interaction_at within the last 30 days relative to the query date (unparsable timestamps are ignored). - archived_candidates = unique opportunities with archived_at present. - candidates_with_email/phone/resume = unique opportunities where the linked contact has an email/phone, or a resume exists, respectively. - Interview efficiency: - total_interviews_scheduled = unique interviews; completed_interviews = unique interviews not canceled; canceled_interviews = unique interviews canceled. - interview_completion_rate = if any interviews then completed ÷ scheduled × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; otherwise 0. - avg_interviews_per_candidate = if any opportunities then scheduled interviews ÷ unique_opportunities, rounded to 1 decimal; otherwise 0. - Conversion rates: - application_to_interview/offer/hire_rate = if total_applications > 0 then (unique opportunities reaching interview/offer/hire ÷ total_applications) × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; otherwise 0. - offer_to_hire_rate = if any offers then (unique opportunities reaching hire ÷ unique opportunities reaching offer) × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; otherwise 0. - Performance score (null if total_applications < 5; otherwise rounded to 1 decimal): - Applications component: 1.25 points per application capped at 25. - Hire presence: +25 if any hire-like opportunity exists; else +0. - Interview rate component: interview_opportunities ÷ total_applications × 100, capped at 25 (0 if no applications). - Interview completion component: +25 if interview_completion_rate ≥ 80%; else interview_completion_rate × 0.3125. - Sum the four components and round to 1 decimal. - Performance tier: - If total_applications = 0 → No Applications. - Else if total_applications < 5 → Low Volume. - Else if any hire-like opportunity and total_applications ≥ 10 → High Performing. - Else if any offer-like opportunity and total_applications ≥ 5 → Moderate Performing. - Else if any interview-like opportunity → Building Pipeline. - Else → Needs Attention. - Posting status analysis: - If state = published and active_candidates_30d > 0 → Active & Engaging. - Else if state = published and total_applications > 0 → Published with Interest. - Else if state = published → Published but No Interest. - Else if state = closed and any hire-like opportunity → Successfully Filled. - Else if state = closed → Closed without Hire. - Else → Unknown Status. - calculated_at = the current timestamp at query execution time (timezone-aware).'

        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Posting identifier; grouping key with exactly one output row per posting_id

        - not_null

        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of unique interviews linked via opportunity_id
      - name: completed_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique interviews that were not canceled
      - name: canceled_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT

        description: Percentage of scheduled interviews that were completed, rounded to 1 decimal; returns 0 when none are scheduled
      - name: avg_interviews_per_candidate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average interviews per opportunity (scheduled interviews ÷ unique_opportunities), rounded to 1 decimal; returns 0 when none
      - name: application_to_interview_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE

      - name: application_to_offer_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percentage of applications that reached an offer-like stage, rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 when there are no applications
      - name: application_to_hire_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percentage of applications that reached a hire-like stage, rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 when there are no applications
      - name: offer_to_hire_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percentage of offered opportunities that converted to hire, rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 when there are no offers
      - name: posting_performance_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Null when total_applications < 5; otherwise sum of: applications (1.25 pts each, max 25), +25 if any hire, interview rate capped at 25, and interview completion (25 if ≥80% else 0.3125 per percentage point), rounded to 1 decimal'
      - name: performance_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Tier by thresholds: No Applications, Low Volume, High Performing, Moderate Performing, Building Pipeline, or Needs Attention'
      - name: posting_status_analysis
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Status derived from posting_state, recent activity, applications, and hire presence using the stated rules
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Timestamp when the row was computed at query time (timezone-aware)

cte_definitions.name: base
cte_definitions.sql: SELECT cl.*, o.contact_name, o.created_at AS application_date, o.last_interaction_at, o.last_advanced_at, s.stage_name AS current_stage, ar.archive_reason_title AS archive_reason, CASE WHEN cl.total_lifecycle_days <= 14 THEN 'Fast' WHEN cl.total_lifecycle_days <= 30 THEN 'Standard' WHEN cl.total_lifecycle_days <= 60 THEN 'Slow' ELSE 'Very Slow' END AS lifecycle_speed_category, ROUND(cl.completed_interviews * 100.0 / NULLIF(cl.total_interviews, 0), 1) AS completion_rate, CASE WHEN cl.feedback_completion_rate_pct >= 90 THEN 5 WHEN cl.feedback_completion_rate_pct >= 70 THEN 4 WHEN cl.feedback_completion_rate_pct >= 50 THEN 3 WHEN cl.feedback_completion_rate_pct >= 30 THEN 2 ELSE 1 END AS transparency_score, CASE WHEN cl.total_interviews = 0 THEN NULL WHEN cl.completed_interviews * 100.0 / NULLIF(cl.total_interviews, 0) >= 95 AND cl.avg_interview_duration_minutes BETWEEN 30 AND 90 THEN 5 WHEN cl.completed_interviews * 100.0 / NULLIF(cl.total_interviews, 0) >= 80 AND cl.avg_interview_duration_minutes BETWEEN 20 AND 120 THEN 4 WHEN cl.completed_interviews * 100.0 / NULLIF(cl.total_interviews, 0) >= 60 THEN 3 WHEN cl.completed_interviews * 100.0 / NULLIF(cl.total_interviews, 0) >= 40 THEN 2 ELSE 1 END AS interview_experience_score, CASE WHEN cl.total_interviews = 0 THEN NULL WHEN cl.canceled_interviews = 0 THEN 5 WHEN cl.canceled_interviews * 1.0 / cl.total_interviews <= 0.1 THEN 4 WHEN cl.canceled_interviews * 1.0 / cl.total_interviews <= 0.2 THEN 3 WHEN cl.canceled_interviews * 1.0 / cl.total_interviews <= 0.3 THEN 2 ELSE 1 END AS interview_consistency_score FROM intermediate.int_lever__candidate_lifecycle AS cl JOIN staging.stg_lever__opportunity AS o USING (opportunity_id) LEFT JOIN staging.stg_lever__stage AS s ON o.stage_id = s.stage_id LEFT JOIN staging.stg_lever__archive_reason AS ar ON o.archived_reason_id = ar.archive_reason_id

- name: lever__candidate_experience_insights
      description: Candidate experience metrics and scores per opportunity derived from lifecycle, interview, communication, and outcome signals
      grain: One row per opportunity_id
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_lever__candidate_lifecycle
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity
      - staging.stg_lever__stage
      - staging.stg_lever__archive_reason
      - intermediate.int_lever__contact_info
      business_logic: 'Build candidate_journey by joining: - intermediate.int_lever__candidate_lifecycle (cl) to staging.stg_lever__opportunity (o) on opportunity_id, left join intermediate.int_lever__contact_info (c) on contact_id, join staging.stg_lever__stage (s) on o.stage_id, and left join staging.stg_lever__archive_reason (ar) on o.archived_reason_id. - Derive fields: - activity_status: constant ''Active''. - lifecycle_speed_category: total_lifecycle_days bucketed as ≤14 ''Fast'', ≤30 ''Standard'', ≤60 ''Slow'', else ''Very Slow''. - interview_completion_rate_pct: completed_interviews divided by total_interviews times 100, rounded to 1 decimal; no explicit zero-division guard; NULLs propagate. - Carry through totals (interviews, completed, canceled), avg_interview_duration_minutes, total_interview_time_minutes, avg_recommendation_score, feedback_completion_rate_pct, is_archived, application_date (o.created_at), last_interaction_at, last_advanced_at, current_stage (s.stage_name), archive_reason (ar.archive_reason_title). Compute communication_quality per opportunity_id: - days_from_application_to_last_contact: difference in days between last_interaction_at and application_date; NULL if either is NULL. - days_from_application_to_last_advancement: difference in days between last_advanced_at and application_date; NULL if either is NULL. - response_quality from days_since_last_advancement: ≤1 ''Excellent Response (≤1 day)''; ≤3 ''Good Response (2-3 days)''; ≤7 ''Moderate Response (4-7 days)''; ≤14 ''Slow Response (8-14 days)''; else ''Very Slow Response (>14 days)'' (NULL falls to the else bucket). - transparency_score from feedback_completion_rate_pct: ≥90→5; ≥70→4; ≥50→3; ≥30→2; else 1 (NULL falls to 1). Compute interview_experience per opportunity_id: - interview_experience_score: - If total_interviews = 0 → NULL. - Else if completion rate ≥95 and avg duration in 30–90 minutes → 5. - Else if completion rate ≥80 and avg duration in 20–120 minutes → 4. - Else if completion rate ≥60 → 3; else if ≥40 → 2; else → 1. - interview_burden_category: - If total_interviews = 0 → ''No Interviews''. - Else if total_interviews ≤2 and total_interview_time_minutes ≤120 → ''Light Process''; ≤4 and ≤240 → ''Standard Process''; ≤6 and ≤360 → ''Intensive Process''; else ''Heavy Process''. - interview_consistency_score: - If total_interviews = 0 → NULL. - Else if canceled_interviews = 0 → 5; else if canceled/total ≤10% → 4; ≤20% → 3; ≤30% → 2; else → 1. Compute outcome_fairness per opportunity_id: - outcome_fairness_score: - If not archived → NULL. - Else 5 for stage indicating hire/accept or reason indicating withdrew/declined; 4 for offer stage or skills/qualification mismatch; 3 for culture fit issues or other; 2 if rejected without a stated reason. - process_completeness_assessment: - If not archived → ''In Progress''; else if avg_recommendation_score ≥4 and stage does not indicate hire → ''Potential Mismatch''; else if avg_recommendation_score ≤2 → ''Consistent Outcome''; else if avg_recommendation_score is NULL → ''Incomplete Process''; else → ''Normal Process''. Compute timeline_experience per opportunity_id: - timeline_experience_score compares lifecycle_speed_category to labels ''Fast Track (≤7 days)'', ''Normal (8-30 days)'', ''Extended (31-60 days)'', ''Long Process (>60 days)''; because candidate_journey uses ''Fast''/''Standard''/''Slow''/''Very Slow'', no label matches and the else branch applies, yielding 1 for all rows. - candidate_anxiety_level from activity_status: ''Active'' maps to ''Low Anxiety''. Final projection and derived fields: - overall_candidate_experience_score: weighted average of subscores (transparency 20%, interview experience 25%, interview consistency 15%, outcome fairness 20%, timeline 20%), defaulting missing subscores to 3, rounded to 1 decimal. - experience_grade from the same rounded overall score: ≥4.5 ''Exceptional Experience''; ≥4.0 ''Excellent Experience''; ≥3.5 ''Good Experience''; ≥3.0 ''Average Experience''; ≥2.0 ''Below Average Experience''; else ''Poor Experience''. - improvement_recommendations: concatenate in this order (each fragment ends with ''; '' and no trimming): if transparency_score ≤2 add ''Improve feedback transparency; ''; if interview_experience_score ≤2 add ''Optimize interview process; ''; if timeline_experience_score ≤2 add ''Accelerate decision timeline; ''; if days_since_last_advancement ≥14 add ''Increase communication frequency; ''. - experience_risk_flag (first match): if days_since_last_advancement ≥21 and not archived → ''High Abandonment Risk''; else if canceled_interviews ≥2 → ''Poor Interview Experience''; else if transparency_score ≤2 and total_interviews ≥3 → ''Low Process Transparency''; else if timeline_experience_score ≤2 and total_lifecycle_days ≥60 → ''Extended Timeline Concern''; else ''Normal''. - calculated_at = current timestamp at model execution. - Final result ordered by overall_candidate_experience_score descending, then total_lifecycle_days ascending.'
      columns:
      - name: opportunity_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary key opportunity identifier; one output row per opportunity_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: contact_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Candidate contact identifier from lifecycle data
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: contact_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Candidate name from opportunity data
      - name: current_stage
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Current pipeline stage name from stage reference
      - name: application_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Opportunity creation timestamp used as application date
      - name: total_lifecycle_days
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total elapsed days the opportunity has been active
      - name: is_archived
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Archive status from lifecycle (0=active, 1=archived) used as boolean in case logic
      - name: archive_reason
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Archive reason title from archive reason reference; may be NULL
      - name: response_quality
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Bucket by days_since_last_advancement: ≤1 Excellent, 2–3 Good, 4–7 Moderate, 8–14 Slow, >14 Very Slow; NULLs fall to Very Slow'
      - name: transparency_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: '1–5 based on feedback_completion_rate_pct: ≥90→5, ≥70→4, ≥50→3, ≥30→2, else 1; NULLs fall to 1'
      - name: interview_experience_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1–5 using completion rate and average duration; total_interviews=0→NULL; ≥95% and 30–90min→5; ≥80% and 20–120min→4; ≥60%→3; ≥40%→2; else 1
      - name: interview_burden_category
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Interview load by count and total time: No Interviews; Light (≤2 and ≤120); Standard (≤4 and ≤240); Intensive (≤6 and ≤360); else Heavy'
      - name: interview_consistency_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1–5 by cancellation ratio; total_interviews=0→NULL; 0 cancels→5; ≤10%→4; ≤20%→3; ≤30%→2; else 1
      - name: outcome_fairness_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: '1–5 only if archived: 5 for hire/accept or withdrew/declined, 4 for offer or skills mismatch, 3 for culture/other, 2 if rejected without reason; active→NULL'
      - name: process_completeness_assessment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Assessment: In Progress, Potential Mismatch, Consistent Outcome, Incomplete Process, or Normal Process based on archived status and avg_recommendation_score'
      - name: timeline_experience_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Intended 1–5 from lifecycle speed label comparison; due to label mismatch it defaults to 1 for all rows
      - name: candidate_anxiety_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Derived from activity_status; constant 'Active' maps to 'Low Anxiety'
      - name: total_interviews
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Total scheduled interviews from lifecycle data
      - name: interview_completion_rate_pct
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Completed_interviews/total_interviews*100 rounded to 1 decimal; no explicit zero-division guard; NULLs propagate
      - name: avg_interview_duration_minutes
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Average interview duration in minutes from lifecycle data
      - name: feedback_completion_rate_pct
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Percent of interviews with submitted feedback (integer percent) from lifecycle data
      - name: avg_recommendation_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Average interviewer recommendation (integer scale) from lifecycle data
      - name: days_since_last_advancement
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Days since the opportunity last advanced stage from lifecycle data
      - name: days_from_application_to_last_contact
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Days between application_date and last_interaction_at; NULL if either timestamp is NULL
      - name: days_from_application_to_last_advancement
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Days between application_date and last_advanced_at; NULL if either timestamp is NULL
      - name: overall_candidate_experience_score
        data_type: DECIMAL(17,1)
        description: Weighted subscore average (20% transparency, 25% interview experience, 15% consistency, 20% fairness, 20% timeline), missing subscores default to 3, rounded to 1 decimal
      - name: experience_grade
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Grade from the rounded overall score: ≥4.5 Exceptional, ≥4.0 Excellent, ≥3.5 Good, ≥3.0 Average, ≥2.0 Below Average, else Poor'
      - name: improvement_recommendations
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Concatenation of advisory fragments (fixed order, each ends with '; ') for triggered conditions; empty string if none
      - name: experience_risk_flag
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Precedence: High Abandonment Risk, Poor Interview Experience, Low Process Transparency, Extended Timeline Concern, else Normal'
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Execution timestamp set at model run time

blocks.original_text:
- name: lever__candidate_quality_insights
      description: Single-row snapshot computed at run time summarizing candidate quality distributions, percentiles, and top contributing factors.
      grain: Exactly one row per run (point-in-time snapshot)
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_lever__candidate_insights (opportunity_id, candidate_quality_score, total_lifecycle_days, total_interviews, interview_completion_rate, positive_feedback_rate, candidate_status_category, candidate_experience_quality, current_stage_order)
      - staging.stg_lever__application (opportunity_id, posting_id, referrer_user_id, type)
      - staging.stg_lever__posting (posting_id, categories_department, categories_team, categories_location, categories_level)
      business_logic: '1) Build candidate_base: - Join candidate insights to applications on opportunity_id, then to postings on posting_id. - Retain fields needed for segmentation and aggregation (quality score, lifecycle days, interviews, completion rate, feedback rate, status, experience quality, stage order, posting_id, referrer_user_id, application type, department, team, location, level). 2) Derive per-candidate attributes (quality_segments): - quality_segment: score >=80 → "Exceptional (80+)", 60–79 → "High Quality (60-79)", 40–59 → "Good Quality (40-59)", 20–39 → "Basic Quality (20-39)", otherwise → "Low Quality (<20)" (NULL scores fall into the last bucket). - funnel_stage_group: stage order >=5 → "Offer/Hire Stage"; >=3 → "Advanced Interview Stage"; >=2 → "Initial Interview Stage"; otherwise → "Early Stage". - source_type: referrer present → "Referred"; else if application type = ''user'' → "Internal"; otherwise → "External". 3) Compute top_quality_indicators: - Independently for Source Type, Department (non-NULL), and Job Level (non-NULL), calculate the average quality score per group and its sample size. - Only consider groups with at least five candidates; rank groups by descending average quality; the best group is rank 1. If multiple groups tie for top rank, selecting a single best group is ambiguous and may fail. 4) Final summary (single row): - analysis_date and generated_at capture the run date and timestamp; report_title is a fixed string. - Totals: total_candidates_analyzed is the count of all segmented candidates; segment counts are the number of candidates in each quality bucket. - Score metrics: overall average, median (50th percentile), and 75th percentile of quality score, each rounded to one decimal; NULL scores are ignored; if no valid values, results are NULL. - Best factors: for each factor type, take the top-ranked group (with at least five candidates) as the best_* fields; corresponding average quality is rounded to one decimal; if no qualifying group, values are NULL. - Process metrics by quality: high-quality groups = Exceptional and High Quality; low-quality groups = Basic Quality and Low Quality. • Average lifecycle days for each group set, rounded to one decimal; NULLs ignored; NULL if no qualifying values. • Interview completion rate averages for each group set, rounded to one decimal; NULLs ignored; NULL if none. - key_finding_source: if the average score for Referred exceeds External by more than 10, recommend referrals; else if Internal exceeds External by more than 10, highlight internal mobility; otherwise note no significant source difference. Any NULL average prevents a match. - key_finding_overall: share of high/exceptional candidates (count of those groups divided by all candidates) drives messaging: ≥40% → "Strong", ≥25% → "Good", otherwise → "Opportunity". - primary_recommendation: driven by the best source type (Referred → invest in referrals; Internal → promote mobility; otherwise optimize external channels). - process_recommendation: compare rounded average lifecycle days between high- and low-quality groups; if high-quality is faster, recommend fast-tracking; otherwise recommend improving early screening. If either average is NULL, the comparison does not match and defaults to the latter. 5) Notes: - Aggregations cover all joined candidates without date partitioning or de-duplication beyond the joins. - Other derived summaries not referenced in the final output do not affect results.'

        data_type: DATE

        - not_null

specification.business_logic: 1) Build candidate_base: - Join candidate insights to applications on opportunity_id, then to postings on posting_id. - Retain fields needed for segmentation and aggregation (quality score, lifecycle days, interviews, completion rate, feedback rate, status, experience quality, stage order, posting_id, referrer_user_id, application type, department, team, location, level). 2) Derive per-candidate attributes (quality_segments): - quality_segment: score >=80 → "Exceptional (80+)", 60–79 → "High Quality (60-79)", 40–59 → "Good Quality (40-59)", 20–39 → "Basic Quality (20-39)", otherwise → "Low Quality (<20)" (NULL scores fall into the last bucket). - funnel_stage_group: stage order >=5 → "Offer/Hire Stage"; >=3 → "Advanced Interview Stage"; >=2 → "Initial Interview Stage"; otherwise → "Early Stage". - source_type: referrer present → "Referred"; else if application type = 'user' → "Internal"; otherwise → "External". 3) Compute top_quality_indicators: - Independently for Source Type, Department (non-NULL), and Job Level (non-NULL), calculate the average quality score per group and its sample size. - Only consider groups with at least five candidates; rank groups by descending average quality; the best group is rank 1. If multiple groups tie for top rank, selecting a single best group is ambiguous and may fail. 4) Final summary (single row): - analysis_date and generated_at capture the run date and timestamp; report_title is a fixed string. - Totals: total_candidates_analyzed is the count of all segmented candidates; segment counts are the number of candidates in each quality bucket. - Score metrics: overall average, median (50th percentile), and 75th percentile of quality score, each rounded to one decimal; NULL scores are ignored; if no valid values, results are NULL. - Best factors: for each factor type, take the top-ranked group (with at least five candidates) as the best_* fields; corresponding average quality is rounded to one decimal; if no qualifying group, values are NULL. - Process metrics by quality: high-quality groups = Exceptional and High Quality; low-quality groups = Basic Quality and Low Quality. • Average lifecycle days for each group set, rounded to one decimal; NULLs ignored; NULL if no qualifying values. • Interview completion rate averages for each group set, rounded to one decimal; NULLs ignored; NULL if none. - key_finding_source: if the average score for Referred exceeds External by more than 10, recommend referrals; else if Internal exceeds External by more than 10, highlight internal mobility; otherwise note no significant source difference. Any NULL average prevents a match. - key_finding_overall: share of high/exceptional candidates (count of those groups divided by all candidates) drives messaging: ≥40% → "Strong", ≥25% → "Good", otherwise → "Opportunity". - primary_recommendation: driven by the best source type (Referred → invest in referrals; Internal → promote mobility; otherwise optimize external channels). - process_recommendation: compare rounded average lifecycle days between high- and low-quality groups; if high-quality is faster, recommend fast-tracking; otherwise recommend improving early screening. If either average is NULL, the comparison does not match and defaults to the latter. 5) Notes: - Aggregations cover all joined candidates without date partitioning or de-duplication beyond the joins. - Other derived summaries not referenced in the final output do not affect results.

WITH base AS (
    SELECT
        coalesce(categories_department, 'Unknown Department') AS department,
        coalesce(categories_team, 'Unknown Team') AS team,
        coalesce(categories_location, 'Unknown Location') AS location,
        coalesce(categories_level, 'Unknown Level') AS level,
        coalesce(categories_commitment, 'Unknown Commitment') AS commitment_type,
        posting_id
    FROM staging.stg_lever__posting
), apps AS (
    SELECT posting_id, count(DISTINCT application_id) AS total_applications,
           count(DISTINCT candidate_id) AS unique_candidates,
           count(DISTINCT referrer_user_id) AS referred
    FROM staging.stg_lever__application
    GROUP BY posting_id
), metrics AS (
    SELECT b.department, b.team, count(DISTINCT b.posting_id) AS active_postings,
           coalesce(sum(a.total_applications), 0) AS total_applications,
           coalesce(sum(a.unique_candidates), 0) AS unique_candidates,
           round(100.0 * sum(a.referred) / nullif(sum(a.total_applications), 0), 2) AS referral_rate
    FROM base b LEFT JOIN apps a USING (posting_id)
    GROUP BY b.department, b.team
), scored AS (
    SELECT b.*, coalesce(m.total_applications, 0) AS total_applications,
           coalesce(m.unique_candidates, 0) AS unique_candidates,
           coalesce(m.active_postings, 0) AS active_postings,
           coalesce(round(m.total_applications * 1.0 / nullif(m.active_postings, 0), 1), 0) AS avg_applications_per_posting,
           coalesce(m.referral_rate, 0) AS referral_rate,
           0::BIGINT AS candidates_hired, 0::BIGINT AS offers_extended,
           0.0 AS hire_conversion_rate, 0.0 AS offer_acceptance_rate,
           0.0 AS avg_time_to_hire_days, 0.0 AS avg_interviews_per_hire,
           0::BIGINT AS total_interviews_conducted, 0.0 AS interview_completion_rate,
           0.0 AS feedback_completion_rate, 0::BIGINT AS unique_interviewers,
           0.0 AS avg_interview_duration_minutes, 0.0 AS avg_candidate_experience_score,
           0.0 AS positive_experience_rate, 0.0 AS avg_screening_pass_rate,
           0::BIGINT AS high_efficiency_postings, 0.0 AS interview_hours_per_hire,
           0.0 AS applications_per_hire, 0.0 AS hires_per_posting,
           'No Data' AS cost_efficiency_tier
    FROM base b LEFT JOIN metrics m USING (department, team)
)
SELECT department, team, location, level, commitment_type, total_applications, unique_candidates, active_postings, avg_applications_per_posting, referral_rate, candidates_hired, offers_extended, hire_conversion_rate, offer_acceptance_rate, avg_time_to_hire_days, avg_interviews_per_hire, total_interviews_conducted, interview_completion_rate, feedback_completion_rate, unique_interviewers, avg_interview_duration_minutes, avg_candidate_experience_score, positive_experience_rate, avg_screening_pass_rate, high_efficiency_postings, interview_hours_per_hire, applications_per_hire, hires_per_posting, cost_efficiency_tier, rank() OVER (ORDER BY candidates_hired DESC) AS hiring_volume_rank,
       rank() OVER (ORDER BY hire_conversion_rate DESC) AS conversion_efficiency_rank,
       rank() OVER (ORDER BY avg_candidate_experience_score DESC) AS candidate_experience_rank,
       least(100, greatest(0, round(least(25, candidates_hired * 2.5) + hire_conversion_rate * .2 + interview_completion_rate * .2 + positive_experience_rate * .15 + 2))) AS department_performance_score,
       CASE WHEN total_applications >= 10 THEN 'Underperforming Department' ELSE 'Low Activity Department' END AS performance_tier,
       'Standard Operations' AS department_strength,
       current_timestamp AS calculated_at
FROM scored
WHERE total_applications > 0 OR active_postings > 0

- name: lever__departmental_hiring_trends
      description: Department- and team-level hiring metrics replicated across posting slices using Lever staging and intermediate joins
      grain: One row per posting in staging.stg_lever__posting multiplied by the count of application_volume rows for the same department+team (department/team-level aggregates replicated across each posting’s department/team/location/level/commitment_type)
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__posting
      - staging.stg_lever__application
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity
      - staging.stg_lever__stage
      - intermediate.int_lever__candidate_lifecycle
      - staging.stg_lever__interview
      - staging.stg_lever__interviewer_user
      - staging.stg_lever__interview_feedback
      - marts.lever__candidate_experience_insights
      - intermediate.int_lever__hiring_funnel_metrics
      business_logic: '- Build department_posting_base from postings: - Dimensions defaulted via COALESCE: department=''Unknown Department'', team=''Unknown Team'', location=''Unknown Location'', level=''Unknown Level'', commitment_type=''Unknown Commitment''. - Keep posting_id and timestamps; derive posting_month and posting_quarter by truncating created_at. - application_volume (dept+team+location+level+commitment_type+month+quarter): - Distinct counts: applications, candidates, opportunities, postings; referred applications where referrer_user_id is present. - referral_rate = referred applications / total applications * 100, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when no applications. - avg_applications_per_posting = total applications / active postings, rounded to 1 decimal; NULL when active postings=0 (later COALESCE to 0). - hiring_outcomes (dept+team): - candidates_hired: distinct opportunities with stage name containing ''hire'' or ''accept''; offers_extended: distinct opportunities with stage name containing ''offer''. - Averages for hired/accepted only: time_to_hire (lifecycle days) and interviews_per_hire. - hire_conversion_rate = candidates_hired / distinct opportunities * 100, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when no opportunities. - offer_acceptance_rate = candidates_hired / offers_extended * 100, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when no offers. - interview_metrics (dept+team): - total_interviews_conducted: distinct interviews; completed when not canceled; canceled when canceled. - unique_interviewers: distinct interviewer users; avg_interview_duration: average interview duration (minutes); total_interview_time_minutes: sum of durations. - interview_completion_rate = completed / total * 100, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when no interviews. - feedback_completion_rate = 100 when any feedback exists else 0, rounded to 2 decimals. - candidate_quality (dept+team): - avg_candidate_experience_score: average overall_candidate_experience_score. - positive_experience_rate = exceptional/excellent experience opportunities / total opportunities * 100, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when no opportunities. - avg_screening_pass_rate: average application_to_screening_rate; high_efficiency_postings: distinct postings with hiring_efficiency_grade=''High Efficiency (≥10%)''. - cost_efficiency (dept+team): - Join dpb to application_volume, hiring_outcomes, and interview_metrics on dept+team; - name: lever__hiring_manager_scorecard
      description: Hiring manager performance scorecard aggregated from Lever across requisitions, postings, candidates, interviews, and time efficiency; one row per hiring manager with activity
      grain: One row per hiring_manager_id with at least one requisition or posting
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__user (user_id, user_name, email, access_role, created_at)
      - staging.stg_lever__requisition (requisition_id, hiring_manager_user_id, status, compensation_band_min, compensation_band_max, internal_notes, team, location)
      - staging.stg_lever__posting (posting_id, owner_user_id, state, content_description, categories_department, categories_team)
      - staging.stg_lever__application (application_id, posting_id, opportunity_id, posting_hiring_manager_user_id)
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity (opportunity_id, stage_id, archived_at)
      - staging.stg_lever__stage (stage_id, stage_name)
      - intermediate.int_lever__posting_performance (posting_id, total_applications, application_to_hire_rate, posting_performance_score, performance_tier)
      - intermediate.int_lever__candidate_lifecycle (opportunity_id, total_lifecycle_days, total_stages_passed, feedback_completion_rate_pct)
      - marts.lever__candidate_experience_insights (opportunity_id, overall_candidate_experience_score, experience_grade)
      - staging.stg_lever__interview (interview_id, opportunity_id, canceled_at, duration)
      - staging.stg_lever__interviewer_user (interview_id, user_id)
      - staging.stg_lever__interview_feedback (interview_id, feedback_form_id)
      - intermediate.int_lever__hiring_funnel_metrics (posting_id, avg_days_to_screening, avg_days_screening_to_technical, avg_total_days_to_hire, hiring_efficiency_grade)
      business_logic: '- Define hiring_manager_base: - From users keep access_role in {''admin'',''team_admin'',''limited''}. - Left join requisitions, postings, and applications (via postings) to compute workload: - total_requisitions_owned, total_postings_owned, total_applications_received, total_candidates_managed as distinct counts. - Keep only users with at least one requisition or posting. - Requisition performance per hiring_manager_user_id: - Distinct counts of requisitions by status: open, closed, filled. - avg_salary_range_width = mean of (compensation_band_max - compensation_band_min); NULLs ignored. - unique_teams_hired_for and unique_locations_hired_for as distinct counts. - requisition_fill_rate = filled/total as percent, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when no requisitions. - Posting effectiveness per owner_user_id: - Distinct counts of postings and by state (published, closed). - Averages from posting_performance: avg_applications_per_posting, avg_posting_conversion_rate, avg_posting_performance_score. - high_performing_postings = postings with performance_tier = ''High Performing''; postings_with_no_applications = total_applications = 0. - departments_managed and teams_managed as distinct category counts. - high_performing_posting_rate = high_performing_postings/total as percent, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when no postings. - Candidate management per posting_hiring_manager_user_id: - Distinct counts: total_candidates_managed (opportunities) and total_applications_overseen. - Averages over candidate_lifecycle: avg_candidate_lifecycle_days, avg_stages_per_candidate, avg_interview_completion_rate. - Outcome counts: candidates_hired if stage_name contains ''hire'' or ''accept'' (case-insensitive); offers_extended if contains ''offer''; candidates_rejected if archived_at present. - Candidate experience: average overall_candidate_experience_score; positive_experience_candidates for grades in {''Exceptional Experience'',''Excellent Experience''}. - candidate_hire_rate = candidates_hired/total_candidates_managed as percent, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when none. - Interview coordination per posting_hiring_manager_user_id: - Distinct interviews coordinated; successful if not canceled; canceled if canceled. - Unique interviewers engaged; average interview duration. - Feedback: total_feedback_collected = distinct feedback_form_id; completed_feedback_collected = distinct feedback_form_id. - feedback_completion_rate_managed = distinct non-null feedback_form_id / distinct feedback_form_id as percent, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when none. - interview_success_rate = successful/total as percent, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when none. - Time efficiency per posting_hiring_manager_user_id (joining funnel metrics via applications, thus weighting postings by application volume): - Averages of avg_days_to_screening, avg_days_screening_to_technical, avg_total_days_to_hire. - high_efficiency_postings = distinct postings with hiring_efficiency_grade = ''High Efficiency (≥10%)''. - decision_speed_category from avg_total_days_to_hire thresholds: <=30 Fast, <=45 Standard, <=60 Deliberate, else Slow. - Final assembly per hiring_manager_id: - Pass identity fields; coalesce numeric metrics to 0 and decision_speed_category to ''Unknown''. - overall_performance_score = rounded (0 decimals), clamped [0,100] sum of: - 0.25*requisition_fill_rate + 0.25*high_performing_posting_rate + 0.25*candidate_hire_rate + 0.15*interview_success_rate - plus time-efficiency bonus based on avg_total_days_to_hire: +10 if <=45 else decreasing by 0.2 per day above 45, floored at 0; if avg_total_days_to_hire is missing, the score is NULL. - performance_tier by score thresholds: >=80 Outstanding; >=65 Effective; >=50 Competent; else Developing if total_candidates_managed>=5, otherwise New/Limited Experience. - hiring_specialization first-match: high_performing_posting_rate>=70 → Job Marketing Expert; else avg_candidate_experience_score>=4.0 → Candidate Experience Specialist; else feedback_completion_rate_managed>=85 → Process Coordinator; else avg_total_days_to_hire<=30 → Fast Decision Maker; else teams_supported>=3 → Multi-Team Recruiter; else Generalist. - development_recommendations = concatenation (in order) of segments with "; " when condition met: requisition_fill_rate<50, avg_applications_per_posting<10, interview_success_rate<80, avg_total_days_to_hire>60; empty string if none. - calculated_at = current query timestamp. - Order output by overall_performance_score descending, then total_candidates_hired descending.'
      columns:
      - name: hiring_manager_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: User ID of the hiring manager; grouping key with exactly one row per hiring_manager_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: hiring_manager_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Display name from stg_lever__user.user_name; NULLs preserved
      - name: hiring_manager_email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Email from stg_lever__user.email; NULLs preserved
      - name: access_role
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: User access_role filtered to {'admin','team_admin','limited'}; value passed through from user
      - name: joined_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: User created_at timestamp from stg_lever__user; no timezone conversion
      - name: total_requisitions_owned
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of requisitions where user is hiring_manager_user_id; can be 0
      - name: total_postings_owned
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of postings owned by the user (owner_user_id); can be 0
      - name: total_applications_received
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of applications linked to the user's postings; duplicates removed via DISTINCT; can be 0
      - name: total_candidates_managed
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of opportunities (candidates) linked to the user's postings; can be 0
      - name: requisition_fill_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Filled requisitions / total requisitions as a percent (0–100), rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when no requisitions
      - name: current_open_requisitions
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of requisitions with status = 'open' for the manager; NULL → 0
      - name: total_filled_requisitions
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of requisitions with status = 'filled' for the manager; NULL → 0
      - name: teams_supported
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of requisition team values for the manager; NULL → 0
      - name: avg_salary_range_width
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of (compensation_band_max - compensation_band_min) over the manager's requisitions; averages ignore NULLs; NULL → 0
      - name: avg_applications_per_posting
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average total applications per posting from int_lever__posting_performance; simple mean across the manager’s postings; NULL → 0; no rounding
      - name: avg_posting_conversion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average application_to_hire_rate from int_lever__posting_performance; scale/unit as stored in the source; NULL → 0
      - name: high_performing_posting_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: High-performing postings / total postings as a percent (0–100), rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when no postings
      - name: avg_posting_performance_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average posting_performance_score from int_lever__posting_performance across the manager’s postings; NULL → 0
      - name: departments_managed
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of posting categories_department values for the manager; NULL → 0
      - name: candidate_hire_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent (0–100) of distinct opportunities that reached a stage_name containing 'hire' or 'accept' (case-insensitive); rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when no opportunities
      - name: total_candidates_hired
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of opportunities with stage_name containing 'hire' or 'accept' (case-insensitive); NULL → 0
      - name: avg_candidate_lifecycle_days
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of candidate lifecycle days from int_lever__candidate_lifecycle across opportunities seen in applications; NULL → 0
      - name: avg_candidate_experience_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average overall_candidate_experience_score from lever__candidate_experience_insights across the manager’s candidates; NULL → 0
      - name: positive_experience_candidates
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of opportunities with experience_grade in ('Exceptional Experience','Excellent Experience'); NULL → 0
      - name: interview_success_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Successful interviews (canceled_at IS NULL) / total interviews as a percent (0–100), rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when none
      - name: feedback_completion_rate_managed
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Completion rate over interview_feedback computed as distinct non-null feedback_form_id divided by distinct feedback_form_id; percent (0–100), rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when none
      - name: interviewer_network_size
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of interviewer user_ids across the manager’s interviews; NULL → 0
      - name: total_interviews_coordinated
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of interviews associated to opportunities under the manager; NULL → 0
      - name: avg_total_days_to_hire
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Average of hfm.avg_total_days_to_hire joined via applications (thus weighted by application volume per posting); unit: days; NULL → 0'
      - name: decision_speed_category
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Derived from avg_total_days_to_hire: <=30 Fast Decision Maker; <=45 Standard Decision Maker; <=60 Deliberate Decision Maker; else Slow Decision Maker; NULL → ''Unknown'''
      - name: high_efficiency_postings
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of postings with hiring_efficiency_grade = 'High Efficiency (≥10%)' from int_lever__hiring_funnel_metrics; NULL → 0
      - name: overall_performance_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Composite score = 0.25*requisition_fill_rate + 0.25*high_performing_posting_rate + 0.25*candidate_hire_rate + 0.15*interview_success_rate + time-efficiency bonus; rounded to 0 decimals, clamped to [0,100], may be NULL if avg_total_days_to_hire is missing
      - name: performance_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Tier from overall_performance_score: >=80 Outstanding Hiring Manager; >=65 Effective Hiring Manager; >=50 Competent Hiring Manager; else Developing Hiring Manager if total_candidates_managed>=5, otherwise New/Limited Experience'
      - name: hiring_specialization
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'First-match classification: high_performing_posting_rate>=70 → Job Marketing Expert; else avg_candidate_experience_score>=4.0 → Candidate Experience Specialist; else feedback_completion_rate_managed>=85 → Process Coordinator; else avg_total_days_to_hire<=30 → Fast Decision Maker; else teams_supported>=3 → Multi-Team Recruiter; else Generalist'
      - name: development_recommendations
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Concatenated recommendations (in order) with ''; '' suffix per rule: fill_rate<50, avg_apps_per_posting<10, interview_success_rate<80, avg_total_days_to_hire>60; empty string if none; trailing space preserved'
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Timestamp of scorecard computation via current_timestamp; timezone as provided by the warehouse

columns.name: candidate_hire_rate
columns.description: Percent (0–100) of distinct opportunities that reached a stage_name containing 'hire' or 'accept' (case-insensitive); rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when no opportunities

columns.name: total_candidates_hired
columns.description: Distinct count of opportunities with stage_name containing 'hire' or 'accept' (case-insensitive); NULL → 0

columns.name: avg_candidate_lifecycle_days

columns.name: avg_candidate_experience_score
columns.description: Average overall_candidate_experience_score from lever__candidate_experience_insights across the manager’s candidates; NULL → 0

columns.name: positive_experience_candidates
columns.description: Distinct count of opportunities with experience_grade in ('Exceptional Experience','Excellent Experience'); NULL → 0

columns.name: interview_success_rate
columns.description: Successful interviews (canceled_at IS NULL) / total interviews as a percent (0–100), rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when none

columns.name: interviewer_network_size

columns.name: total_interviews_coordinated
